items.text: Changed: **the clean screen no longer pops out from a stray touch.** A tap outside the grid does nothing now. Press and hold there and a light, see-through band of the accent colour rises from the bottom of the screen; when it fills the screen the controls come back. Let go early and it sinks away. Escape still leaves at once.

**more than one shape on the field.** In the G-code panel, a *Shapes* row adds an ellipse, triangle, square, diamond, line or wave, or *+ Drawing* for a second G-code drawing. Up to six, beside the main drawing.

Each shape has its own cross, diamond and arc handles and its own motion (turn, size, move, and how fast). Tap a shape's line and the tether bar opens for it: three motion tiles, speed, *sound* (puts a sound on it) and *remove*. Arrows step from shape to shape.
Sounds ride any shape: *still*, *wander* or *follow* (a line or wave is travelled out and back). Drop a sound near any shape and it snaps on; removing a shape lets its sounds go where they are.
Shapes are remembered between visits.
Not yet: vertex effects on the extra shapes (they stay on the main drawing).

**the tether bar replaces the rings** in the G-code editor. Tap a vertex, a sound, one of the drawing's handles, or the field (for the whole drawing) and one small, see-through bar floats beside it, joined to it by a dotted line. It keeps off the object and stays inside the field.

Each tile shows how much of something is on with a bar under it. Drag across a tile to change it (level, tone, space, effect amount, reach, span, how many); tap a tile with choices to step through them (sound, movement, effect). The tiles for a vertex, a sound, the drawing and a handle are each their own.

**Arrows jump from object to object** along the drawing, and wrap round. The scope tile picks what they visit: vertices, sounds only, or only the marked ones (vertices with a sound or an effect). Stay in one bar and edit them all.

**Handles run by themselves.** Tap the turn, size or move handle: turn is still, left, right, bounce or random; size is still, pulse, saw, jump or random; move is still, drift, orbit, sway or wander; plus slow, medium or fast. They add up, and a handle running a motion gets a dashed ring. Pick still and the drawing stays where it got to.
Changed: two quick taps on a sound no longer take it away (it opens its bar; use *remove*, and Undo brings it back).

**out and back**. Every play line has a new switch, *Way runs*: set it to "Out and back, like a tide" and the line goes to the far end, then comes home the same way instead of starting again. The far end sounds once, so a way of twelve cells becomes a pass of twenty-two. Each line has its own switch, so one can bounce while another runs through.
New line-ups: **Shoreline** (one bouncing line) and **Two tides** (two bouncing lines at 3:2, so the waves cross and drift in and out of step).
Changed: **Tide** now really is a tide: it bounces. It used to be a plain upward line with a noisy feel.
Saved looks, made pieces, packs and your own line-ups remember which lines bounce.

the drawing has handles, and a ghost twin. In the G-code editor the drawing wears three round handles on a faint ring: the **cross** in the middle moves it, the **diamond** sizes it, the **arc** turns it. Grab one and the drawing in your hand (in the accent colour) stands still while a ghost of it, with its old size, place and movement, keeps playing and carrying the sounds. Let go and the sounds glide over to the new drawing in two seconds, and it carries on from there. Double-tap the cross, or **Put the drawing back** in the panel, to return it to where it started. Its place, size and turn are remembered, and a look you keep carries them.

a sound has a twin too. Open the ring of a moving sound (one with a drawn or wandering movement, or one riding a drawing) and it stands still in your hand, quiet until you change something, while a ghost (a dashed ring) keeps playing its old movement. Close the ring and it takes up the new movement; the ghost plays on for a moment and fades. The ghost is never saved.
Fixed: changing a field sound's voice in its ring no longer drops its movement or its place on a vertex.
The drawings panel is only as tall as it needs to be, so the handles stay reachable below it.

vertex-effect sets. In the drawings panel, under **More**, four made sets put effects on the current drawing in one tap: **Breathe** (every 24th vertex swells the level), **Bright corners** (every 16th brightens the tone), **Glide up** (every 32nd bends the note up) and **Room at the ends** (the first and last vertices add space). **Keep set** saves what the current drawing's vertices do under a name; tap it later to put it on any drawing (every drawing has the same 96 vertices). Hold one of yours to delete it.

Changed: the G-code ring is small now, with a centre. It opens with a middle that says what you are editing (**Drawing**, or **Vertex 41**) and three or four dots: **sound**, **moves**, **spread** (for the whole drawing) or **effect** and **put here** (for one vertex). Each dot opens a small ring of its own with the controls that used to crowd the first ring: sound has the sound's choice, level, tone and space; moves has still, wander and follow; spread has how many, spread and apply to all; effect has the kind (level, tone, space, pitch), **how much** (amount, reach, span), set here and clear here. The back arrow in the middle goes up one.

Changed: the drawings panel scrolls sideways. The sets and the drawings in the set are two strips you swipe, with the current one centred, instead of a wall of buttons; keeping a drawing and the grid-sound choice are folded under **More**. A tap answers at once: the button gets a turning ring and the panel fades so you can see the field while the drawing loads.

Fixed: the field comes back. The sounds you place on a drawing, each on its vertex, are now saved a moment after any change, with the drawing, and put back at your first touch the next time you open Battanboo (browsers only let sound start on a touch). Before, only the drawing and its vertex effects were remembered.
**pitch** is a vertex effect. A vertex can bend the note of a sound passing near it, up or down by as much as an octave at full amount, fading to nothing at its reach.

**live preview**. While a vertex's effect ring is open, moving amount, reach, span or the kind lets you hear it at once on the sounds near that vertex. It is only kept when you press **set here**; closing the ring drops it.

Fixed: in the G-code editor the rail now keeps the HUD button in the lower corner and puts the G-code tools directly above it, instead of below it. Everything else the mode does not need stays off the rail.
